newsitem.title: UK: UK stocks regain poise but outlook remains choppy.
newsitem.headline: UK stocks regain poise but outlook remains choppy.

text.p: UK shares regained their poise on Friday after a dramatic recovery on Wall Street overnight but the sour start to the New Year may be a sign that the London market is nearing its peak, chart watchers said.
"We're in the final stages of the bull market," said Chris Chaitow, a technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities.
"Whether we can go up another 100 points is hard to predict," he said. "But I'm working on the theory that the next major market move will be down...January may turn out to be disappointing."
The FTSE index stood 26.1 points higher at 4,083.5 by 1508 GMT on Friday, recovering over a third of the previous session's losses after Wall Street roared back from its recent retreat.

The FTSE scrambled to a record high of 4118.5 on the last trading day of 1996, but most strategists are not expecting to see a repeat of this near 12-percent growth in 1997. The average FTSE forecast from strategists for end-1997 is around 4,250.

According to a survey of pension fund activity published by the WM Company this week, fund managers are running higher cash weightings and have already reduced their exposure to UK equities in the belief that stocks are overvalued.
Next week will provide a better guide as to where UK shares may be heading this year, as investors return from extended holidays and trading volumes begin to pick up again.
"The moves so far haven't really meant anything in the grand context of things," Chaitow commented. "There's too little volume for it to matter.
"Next week's performance will be high profile," he added. "January is usually a very indicative month for the rest of the year and the first week in January is quite indicative for the month."
Retailers are likely to be under the spotlight as Britain's major stores begin to release figures from the key Christmas trading period.

In addition, Dixons reports interim results on Wedesday. The shares have outperformed the general market this week on the back of expectations of strong Christmas sales. Argos and Sears follow with their trading statements on Friday.

UK economic news is likely to be overshadowed by U.S. payrolls data on Friday. The volatile performance of U.S. financial markets recently owes much to signs of a strengthening economy and growing fears of rising interest rates.
UK money supply figures kick off the week's data on Monday followed by housing starts on Thursday and industrial production figures on Friday.
In the U.S., other key statistics include consumer credit and producer price figures.
